### Claude Code Review

- [x] Read the new relay route (controller / service / module / DTO)
- [x] Review `WorkspaceRelayer` and `RelaySimulationService`

- [x] Review the migration and any DB/repo changes
- [x] Review the moved `SpaceIdPipe`, `@Auth()`, `assertMember`
- [x] Post consolidated feedback

The arch-review already covered the guide-level items (module boundaries, Swagger completeness, the bare `rejects.toThrow` test). Below are the remaining things I'd flag — focused on correctness, observability, and a small tidy-up. Nothing here is blocking.

---

#### 1. Silent quota bypass when `recordUsage` fails — needs an alert, not just a log

[`workspace.relayer.ts:113-123`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/relay/domain/relayers/workspace.relayer.ts#L113-L123) catches `recordUsage` errors and drops them to a `warn` log. The reasoning ("a relay already made cannot fail because the counter did") is correct — but the failure mode is that a persistent DB fault lets every workspace relay unlimited transactions at your expense, and the only signal is warn-level noise mixed with everything else. Consider:

- Using `error` level, or a dedicated `LogType` (e.g. `LogType.QuotaRecordFailed`) so an alerting rule can key on it directly. Same pattern the `LogType.QuotaExceeded` event already uses in `entitlements.service.ts:227`.
- Or emitting a metric counter so it's graphable, not just log-searchable.

#### 2. `EntitlementsService.recordUsage` silently no-ops when `grant.counter === null`

[`entitlements.service.ts:194-208`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L194-L208) — if the cached grant has `counter: null` for a feature that is `Exclude<FeatureKey, StockMeteredFeature>`, it warns and returns. That's the same silent-bypass shape as #1: a stale/broken cache entry disables usage recording without failing loudly. The interface type already excludes stock-metered keys, so any `null` counter reaching here is unexpected state. Consider throwing instead of returning quietly — the caller in `WorkspaceRelayer` already has an error-catching wrapper around it, so it would still not break the relay, but the failure would be surfaced.

#### 3. Concurrent-admission overshoot is documented — is it monitored?

The PR description calls this out honestly: "concurrent callers being admitted against the same count and together overshooting the allowance." The `incrementUsage` upsert returns the post-increment `used` value ([`space-feature-usage.repository.ts:83-84`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/entitlements/domain/space-feature-usage.repository.ts#L83-L84)) but nothing consumes it. That returned value is exactly what would let you detect the overshoot post-hoc:

```ts
const usedAfter = await this.spaceFeatureUsageRepository.incrementUsage({ ... });
if (grant.quota !== null && usedAfter > grant.quota) {
  this.loggingService.warn({ type: LogType.QuotaOvershoot, ... });
}
```

Not needed to ship, but leaves you blind to how often the trade-off actually bites in production.

#### 4. `SpaceRelayModule` — likely unneeded `forwardRef`s

[`space-relay.module.ts:31-33`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/relay/space-relay.module.ts#L31-L33) wraps `AuthModule`, `SpacesModule`, and `UsersModule` in `forwardRef`. `forwardRef` is only needed when two modules import each other; none of those three imports `SpaceRelayModule`. If Nest doesn't complain, plain imports will work and be clearer. The module docstring already explains why it's a separate module — the `forwardRef`s aren't part of that story.

#### 5. `countFeatureUsage` — synthetic narrowing object

[`entitlements.service.ts:291-295`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/entitlements/routes/entitlements.service.ts#L291-L295) builds `const feature = { key: args.featureKey }` just so the type guard narrows. Small thing, but the guard could take a plain key (`isStockMeteredFeatureKey`) and the object goes away. Not worth a change on its own — mention if you touch this file again.

#### 6. `WorkspaceRelayer` — hardcoded `'workspace'` literal as relayer name

[`workspace.relayer.ts:148`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/4ff1b96c286f5d96a0a733a25e74ee7bb7b127a7/src/modules/relay/domain/relayers/workspace.relayer.ts#L148) passes `relayer: 'workspace'` to `assertRelayable`; `SIMULATED_RELAYERS` in `relay-simulation.service.ts` lives elsewhere. A typo here compiles because the argument type is `SimulatedRelayer` and `'workspace'` happens to be a member — but a symbol-level constant colocated with `SIMULATED_RELAYERS` would remove the "magic string" nit R-018 tends to flag.

---

**Verdict:** ✅ Nothing blocking. Items 1–2 are the ones I'd genuinely address before merge — the silent-bypass paths are the kind of thing that only fires once you're relying on the counter for billing decisions, and by then it's expensive to notice.
